summary: Workflow-backed code review — one finder per correctness angle plus one finder covering all cleanup angles, an independent verifier for every distinct (file, line) location across the pooled candidates, then a ranked, capped findings report.

result.target:
— Review the freshly committed Phase 2 (#221) RC-Dynamik in the TU-Dresden Diplomarbeit cache-engine (C++23, g++-16). This is a scientific Hard-Gate before the multi-day #156 measurement run, so correctness of runtime measurement behavior is paramount. Repo roots: super = /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine ; ce = super/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine. Scope = exactly the last commit on each: ce HEAD 1f9c2eef "4 restliche RC-Achsen an Organe verdrahtet" and super HEAD 2a8c36c "ce-Bump #221". Review these diffs (`git -C <root> show <sha>`).
The change wires 4 Resource-Control axes from the ComdareResourceControlV1 POD to their organs so they take real runtime effect (previously only prefetch_distance was wired; the other 4 were written to applied_rc_ but never reached an organ → "Phantom-Zeilen" at #156). Files: ce libs/cache_engine/anatomy/abi_adapter.hpp (the 4 new `if constexpr (requires { organ_.set_runtime_X(...); })` blocks mirroring the prefetch pattern) + 5 organ headers (axis_08_concurrency_observable.hpp set_runtime_thread_count; axis_04_node_type_layout_aware_store.hpp set_runtime_pool_budget_bytes + copy/move ctor changes; observable_composed_container.hpp + observable_composed_search.hpp set_runtime_batch_size/pool_budget delegation + drive_runtime_batch_probe_; axis_14_value_handle_observable.hpp set_runtime_inline_threshold_bytes) + tests/unit/test_221_rc_remaining_axes.cpp (new DEG test) + 4 builder CMakeLists (CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR->PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR).
FOCUS especially on SCIENTIFIC CORRECTNESS: (1) Is RC=0 TRULY a byte-identical no-op vs. pre-change behavior for EACH of the 4 organs (golden-neutrality)? Look for any code path where the new runtime member or its default 0 subtly alters behavior/measurement even when unset (e.g. changed control flow, extra branches on the hot path, changed struct layout affecting the store's memory footprint measurement, altered copy/move semantics in axis_04 store). (2) Do the non-zero effects create a MEANINGFUL, HONEST runtime signal (real work the axis controls) rather than an ARTIFICIAL/decorative DEG (e.g. does batch_size's "extra Slot-Probe per lookup" measure something real about the traversal axis, or is it fake busy-work that would mislead the thesis)? (3) Does test_221_rc_remaining_axes actually PROVE each axis takes effect (DEG>0 for non-zero, no-op for 0), or is it a weak test? (4) The axis_04 store gained runtime members + rewritten copy/move ctors — any use-after-move, double-count, or state-leak bug? (5) Concurrency organ set_runtime_thread_count driving "acquire/release pairs multiple times" — any correctness/deadlock/measurement-distortion issue? HARD REQUIREMENTS to flag if violated: additive only; golden/ABI-neutral (must NOT change ComdareResourceControlV1 sizeof/layout, golden_fullpilot_320, ABI-MAJOR, GenusBindingTraits); no runtime-switch/vtable in hot path beyond the existing if constexpr requires; no Python. Also flag resource/lifetime bugs and any measurement-integrity risk for the #156 run.
result.summary: Max-effort review of the Phase-2 commit that wires four resource-control axes (batch_size, pool_budget_bytes, thread_count, inline_threshold_bytes) into the #156 measurement; the 29 verified findings collapse to 15 distinct defects. The gravest are correctness/measurement-integrity bugs: silent data loss when a lowered pool budget makes erase/migrate re-append survivors through the now budget-gated append_slot; budget-rejected non-stored inserts still driving every sibling organ so multiple axes over-count; and the flagship batch_size axis broken four independent ways (container for_each_record full-scan that never stops at batch_size, restore_statistics zeroing the probe counters on two-phase rollback, the counters written to nullptr CSV-schema columns so they never reach the output, and masstree silently no-oping without for_each_record). The remainder are the 0-as-sentinel RC latch that prevents returning any axis to default on a reused tier, allocator failure_count contamination with policy rejections, config-gated distortions (pool_budget not applied to pool-family organs, value_handle version/chain-depth suppressed under RC) plus two latent divide-by-zero paths, and low-severity cleanups (write-only checksum/DCE risk, extra hot-path branch).

findings.summary: append_slot gained a budget-rejection early-return (line 203), but rebuild_ (line 467, called by erase_slot_at/insert_slot_at/migrate) still relies on the old invariant that append_slot ALWAYS appends the given slot to faithfully reconstruct the flattened set; that append-always guarantee is now conditional and not re-established in rebuild_. [same root cause also at: /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/node/axis_04_node_type_layout_aware_store.hpp:469, /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/node/axis_04_node_type_layout_aware_store.hpp:234, /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/node/axis_04_node_type_layout_aware_store.hpp:355]
findings.failure_scenario: A tier whose pool_budget_bytes is nonzero and whose live set already exceeds that budget (budget applied/lowered after records were loaded — the guard blocks growth, never shrink) receives an erase: erase_slot_at (line 231) flattens all slots, then rebuild_ does clear() (size_->0) and re-appends via append_slot, which now early-returns as soon as capacity_bytes_for_slot_count_ crosses the budget. Every slot past the budget is silently discarded, so erasing one key drops other still-valid keys — subsequent tier_lookup of those keys returns miss (wrong result / data loss) and tier_size undercounts, corrupting the #156 workload state.

findings.summary: insert() now returns false when the pool budget rejects growth, but abi_adapter::tier_insert (line 840) never checks the return: it unconditionally drives every observer coupling and mutates aux organs (Bloom filter insert_key, value-handle store_value, Patricia insert_key, telemetry/ct/map/q1/q2/cc) for records that were never stored. [same root cause also at: /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/anatomy/abi_adapter.hpp:840]
findings.failure_scenario: At #156, a pool_budget sweep to a small value with an insert-heavy workload causes each budget-rejected insert (record NOT in the main store) to still tick the T1/T2/T3/T7/T8/T10/T16/T17 observer counters and to keep populating the Bloom filter, value-handle pool, and Patricia trie unbounded. Result: per-axis stats over-count relative to the actually-stored data (e.g. filter/traversal register counts = N+rejected while node_type keys_stored = N), and auxiliary memory grows without limit despite the budget, so the 'memory-constrained' regime the pool_budget axis is supposed to measure is invalid — the budget caps only the main store, not total memory.

findings.summary: The `if (visited >= runtime_batch_size_) return;` returns only from the for_each_record lambda, not from the loop, so every lookup scans ALL records regardless of batch_size (the store-backed observable_composed_search path correctly bounds to min(batch_size, n) real slot probes). [same root cause also at: /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/lookup/composable/observable_composed_container.hpp:183, /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/lookup/composable/observable_composed_container.hpp:183, /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/lookup/composable/observable_composed_container.hpp:178, /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/lookup/composable/observable_composed_search.hpp:285]
findings.failure_scenario: For any pool-family tier (container_algorithm_ = ObservableComposedContainer whose Container has for_each_record) at #156, changing batch_size never changes per-lookup traversal cost because each lookup always performs a full O(total-records) scan; the batch_size axis timing signal is flat/insensitive and r[7] (runtime_batch_probe_count) under-reports the real work while r[6] reports the configured batch_size, yielding an invalid, non-comparable, effectively decorative batch_size DEG for those tiers.

findings.summary: restore_statistics() -- the #133 O(1) rollback that is documented to restore the counters EXACTLY to the saved state -- calls reset_runtime_batch_probe_statistics(), zeroing runtime_batch_probe_count_/checksum_ instead of preserving them (same pattern in observable_composed_container.hpp line 157). [same root cause also at: /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/lookup/composable/observable_composed_search.hpp:144, /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/lookup/composable/observable_composed_search.hpp:142, /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/lookup/composable/observable_composed_search.hpp:142]
findings.failure_scenario: If batch_size RC is active and a stats-only tier_rollback_all (which routes through restore_statistics, per abi_adapter) runs during the #156 measurement, runtime_batch_probe_count_ is reset to 0 while the SearchAlgoStatistics are restored to their saved values, so the r[7] batch-probe DEG observed for that tier after any rollback under-reports the cumulative traversal work and diverges from the full-memento restore_state() path which does restore it.

findings.summary: fill_observer_v3 writes runtime_batch_size -> axis_stats[0][6] and runtime_batch_probe_count -> axis_stats[0][7], but kV3AxisSchema[0] (T0) declares nullptr at fields 6 and 7, and every CSV/trace emitter drops nullptr-named fields — so the deterministic batch_size evidence never reaches the #156 output despite the commit's anti-phantom goal. [same root cause also at: /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/anatomy/abi_adapter.hpp:1050]
findings.failure_scenario: At the #156 run, sweeping batch_size on a LayoutAwareChunkedStore composition: cache_engine_builder_iterator.hpp lines 220 and 381 both `continue` on kV3AxisSchema[0].names[6]==nullptr / names[7]==nullptr, and measurement_snapshot.hpp / tier_observe_trace_abi.hpp read only named indices, so no batch_size or batch_probe_count column is ever emitted. The only batch-attributable CSV signal left is the noisy seg_ns[0] timing; the deterministic per-op probe count that RcBatchSize221 asserts on (axis_stats[0][6]==5, [0][7]==15) is invisible in the real output, and the unit test passes only because it reads the in-process POD — masking the gap so the traversal-axis batch_size effect cannot be deterministically attributed in the thesis.

findings.summary: Classic falsy-zero/zero-as-sentinel: apply1 (`if (v != 0) dst = ...`) plus every new set_runtime_* setter (`if (X != 0) member_ = X`) treat 0 as 'keep current', so applied_rc_ and the organ members are sticky and no axis can ever be returned to its 0/default state at runtime on the same tier. [same root cause also at: /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/anatomy/abi_adapter.hpp:228]
findings.failure_scenario: At the multi-day #156 run, if the RuntimeVariableLoop reuses one tier across measurement points and sets axes independently (point A thread_count=8/others 0, point B batch_size=16/others 0), point B still runs with thread_count=8 because 0 never clears the prior value; every row after the first non-zero RC is silently confounded by all previously-set axes, and any point meant to be 'default' (e.g. unlimited pool_budget=0 after a limited one) reproduces the stale limit — yielding wrong DEG rows in the thesis.

findings.summary: allocator_statistics() folds the pool-budget POLICY rejection count into the allocator snapshot's failure_count, which fill_observer_v3 (abi_adapter line 1123) exports as the T6 'fail' CSV column -- so a traversal/node pool_budget RC contaminates the genuine allocator-OOM-failure signal with policy rejections; and because clear() (line 236) never resets runtime_pool_budget_rejections_, the count accumulates monotonically across the tier's lifetime and is re-incremented by every over-budget restore_state re-insert, inflating 'fail' to an arbitrary multiple of the real rejection count.
findings.failure_scenario: In a #156 run with pool_budget RC active, the 5th insert into a one-chunk-budget store is policy-rejected; allocator_statistics() returns failure_count=1 even though std::malloc never failed, and the T6 CSV 'fail' column reads 1 (a phantom allocator failure). Across repeated save/restore rollback cycles the rejection re-fires each cycle because clear() keeps runtime_pool_budget_rejections_, so 'fail' climbs cycle-by-cycle, making the allocator-failure metric unable to distinguish real allocator pressure from budget-policy denials -- a scientist reads it as allocator instability. The new DEG test never exercises multi-cycle accumulation, so it stays green.

findings.summary: The container wrapper's batch probe is fully gated behind `if constexpr (requires { c.for_each_record(...) })` and silently no-ops when the wrapped Container lacks for_each_record, whereas the sibling observable_composed_search wrapper drives the probe unconditionally via store().slot_count()/key_at/value_at.
findings.failure_scenario: At #156, compositions whose container_algorithm_ is an observable_composed_container over a flat Container without for_each_record report runtime_batch_probe_count == 0 for every non-zero batch_size RC, so the batch_size axis shows a phantom 'no effect' for that whole class of rows even though the RC was applied and set_runtime_batch_size stored it — mismeasuring the traversal axis and reintroducing phantom-zero rows for container-backed compositions while store-backed ones show a real signal.

findings.summary: pool_budget_bytes is wired only where container_algorithm_ exposes set_runtime_pool_budget_bytes, which resolves to a real setter only for LayoutAwareChunkedStore (flat-store) compositions; no pool organ (btree/hash/swiss/eytzinger/masstree/wormhole/surf) provides it, so for ObservableComposedContainer<Organ> and organ-hull SearchAlgos the if constexpr(requires{...}) is false and the RC is silently not applied.
findings.failure_scenario: At #156, sweeping pool_budget_bytes across pool-family / organ-hull compositions produces byte-identical rows regardless of the budget value because tier_apply_resource_control's guarded block is compiled out for those container_algorithm_t types (grep confirms only the 3 changed files define set_runtime_pool_budget_bytes / runtime_pool_budget_can_grow_by_one). The very Phantom-Zeilen the commit claims to eliminate persist for every pool-backed member of the 320 lineup, while flat-store families do show an effect — so the thesis reports an inconsistent pool_budget axis with no marker distinguishing the still-phantom rows.

findings.summary: observe_value_handle replaced the unconditional `has_version_tag_()` version-tag counting and `chain_depth_()` depth with effective_has_version_tag_() (false whenever runtime_inline_threshold_bytes_!=0) and effective_chain_depth_() (1 or 2, ignoring the strategy's compile-time chain_depth_), removing the version-tag/chain-depth accounting for the entire RC-override path. [same root cause also at: /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/Code/external/comdare-cache-engine/libs/cache_engine/axes/value_handle_axis/axis_14_value_handle_observable.hpp:167]
findings.failure_scenario: At #156 a tier composed with a versioned-pointer (or multi-level chain) value_handle AND a nonzero inline_threshold_bytes RC: version_tag_strips is gated on effective_has_version_tag_() which returns false for any threshold!=0, and depth comes from effective_chain_depth_() which collapses to 1 or 2 regardless of the strategy's real chain_depth_. The versioned/chained strategy therefore reports version_tag_strips=0 (axis_stats[11][2]) and a collapsed peak_chain_depth/indirect_deref_count for the whole inline_threshold sweep, hiding the MVCC/chain work the T11 value-handle axis is supposed to measure — a phantom-zero introduced in a different axis by the RC wiring.

findings.summary: `start = k % static_cast<key_type>(n)` narrows the size_t slot count to key_type before the modulo; when key_type is narrower than size_t and n is a multiple of 2^width(key_type), the divisor truncates to 0 → division by zero (UB/crash).
findings.failure_scenario: Once StorageOrgan key widths are narrowed (explicitly planned #217-2b, referenced in the key_type comment; e.g. uint8_t key over a 256-slot Array256 store), static_cast<uint8_t>(256)==0 and `k % 0` crashes the measurement binary the first time batch_size>0 RC hits that traversal organ during #156; short of exact truncation the divisor still wraps, shifting the probe start slot. (Latent today: all current StorageOrgans use uint64 key, so no live crash before #217-2b.)

findings.summary: Off-by-one divisor guard in external_handle_scan_: `span >= 3u ? span - 3u : 1u` yields divisor 0 when span==3 (should be `span > 3u`), giving `handle % 0` → modulo-by-zero UB.
findings.failure_scenario: If observe_value_handle is ever driven with n*record_size == 3 (any future narrow-stride value-handle scan, e.g. n=3/record_size=1), the inline_threshold external path divides by zero and crashes the measurement run; currently masked only because value-handle record_size is always >=16.

findings.summary: thread_count is modeled as N sequential acquire/release pairs in a single thread, scaling acquire/release counts by N while contention/validation stay 0.
findings.failure_scenario: With thread_count=3, observe_critical_section runs 3 sequential lock/unlock pairs, so axis_stats[8][0]/[8][1] (acquire/release) scale x3 but axis_stats[8][2]/[8][3] (contention/validation_fail) remain 0. The T8 output at #156 therefore describes a physically impossible '3 concurrent threads with zero contention'; any thesis interpretation of thread_count as real concurrency, or of contention-per-acquire, is misled by a purely sequential repetition dressed up as parallelism.

findings.summary: runtime_batch_probe_checksum_ is write-only in the container wrapper (accumulated and reset but never read/exported), unlike the search wrapper which at least saves it in the memento.
findings.failure_scenario: The container wrapper computes runtime_batch_probe_checksum_ ^= sink on every probe but no code ever reads it, so it is dead state; and because it is the only consumer of the per-record reads (sink ^= k; sink += v), an optimizing g++-16 build may dead-code-eliminate those reads, leaving only ++visited -> the 'real Slot-Probe' would stop touching record memory and the batch DEG would measure bare counter arithmetic instead of the cache traffic it claims. Either export it (like the count) or remove it.

findings.summary: drive_runtime_batch_probe_(k) is called unconditionally on every lookup, adding a member load + compare + branch to the RC=0 golden path.
findings.failure_scenario: The commit claims RC=0 is 'byte-identisches heutiges Verhalten'. The lookup body now always calls drive_runtime_batch_probe_, which begins with 'if (runtime_batch_size_ == 0) return;'. Even with batch_size unset, every lookup at #156 executes an extra load+branch that was not there before, so the golden/RC=0 lookup timing is not the byte-identical no-op asserted. Uniform across RC=0 rows (cancels in comparisons) but the byte-identity claim is overstated.

refuted.summary: append_slot's new growth-budget guard is reached from rebuild_() (used by erase_slot_at and insert_slot_at), so any erase performed while the store's footprint exceeds the current pool_budget_bytes silently discards surviving records — violating the setter's own documented 'bestehende Chunks werden nicht rueckwirkend abgebaut' contract.

Pool-budget enforcement is duplicated: the wrapper insert() checks runtime_pool_budget_accepts_growth_ AND the store re-checks inside append_slot/insert_slot_at, so the budget is smeared across two levels and the rejection counter can be bumped from either.

Non-zero inline_threshold<8 reinterprets the first 4 bytes of each real key/value record as a 'handle' and dereferences a pseudo-random within-buffer offset — synthetic memory traffic not tied to any real value-handle indirection the axis models.
The new test_221 block uses PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR while its 9 sibling blocks in the same file still use CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR, leaving the include-path convention mixed.

The #133 two-phase memento rollback restore_state() -- documented (lines 238-241) to restore the data substrate EXACTLY -- delegates to ComposedSearch::restore_state, which does store_.clear() (clear() at axis_04 line 236 does NOT reset runtime_pool_budget_bytes_) and then re-inserts every saved record via Traversal::insert_into -> append_slot/insert_slot_at, both now budget-gated; so under an active pool_budget RC the whole warm-state restore silently drops its tail. This is a different, more severe caller than the erase_slot_at/insert_slot_at/migrate paths already flagged: it is the loop's reset mechanism itself.
